merge_strategies.notes: NEW SKILL. Strong understanding of three merge strategies: merge commit (preserves full history, two parents), squash and merge (combines all commits into one, clean linear history), rebase and merge (linear history with preserved commits, deferred to Phase 25). Excellent judgment about when to use each: squash for most CatchBook features (clean history), merge commit for security/authentication/major architectural changes (audit trail preservation). Understanding of fast-forward vs three-way merges. Recognition that squash-and-merge is GitHub's recommended default and appropriate for 90% of CatchBook workflow.

merge_conflict_resolution.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent understanding of conflict mechanics: occur when two branches modify same lines in same file, adjacent lines with incompatibilities, or one deletes what other modifies. Successfully completed intentional conflict creation/resolution exercise. Mastery of conflict marker anatomy (<<<<<<< HEAD, =======, >>>>>>> branch-name). Proficient with VS Code conflict resolution UI (Accept Current, Accept Incoming, Accept Both, Compare Changes). Understanding of command-line resolution workflow (git status, manual editing, git add, git commit). Key insight: conflicts aren't disasters, they're decision points requiring synthesis. Recognition that best resolutions often combine both versions rather than choosing binary winner.

git_merge_mechanics.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete understanding of merge process: Git identifies common ancestor (divergence point), compares changes in each branch since divergence, combines changes into new state. Understanding of fast-forward merge (no divergence, target branch just moves forward) vs three-way merge (both branches have new commits, explicit merge commit created). Recognition that three-way merge examines three commits: common ancestor, feature branch tip, target branch tip. Understanding that Git auto-merges far more than expected (different files, different sections, non-overlapping changes) and only stops for ambiguous conflicts.

branch_cleanup.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete mastery of local and remote branch cleanup: git branch -d (safe delete, requires merge), git branch -D (force delete, discards work), git push -d origin branch-name (delete remote branch), git fetch --prune (remove stale remote references). Understanding of when to use safe vs force delete. Recognition that cleanup prevents branch clutter and confusion about active work. Successfully troubleshot branch cleanup issues (stale remote references, ahead/behind warnings). Understanding that GitHub can auto-delete branches on PR merge.

post_merge_workflow.notes: NEW SKILL. Identified critical post-merge ritual as top muscle-memory priority: checkout main → pull origin main → delete merged branch → checkout new feature branch. Understanding that skipping 'pull main' causes working from outdated base, leading to unnecessary conflicts with own merged work. Recognition that this sequence should become automatic like Cmd+S. Understanding that consistent rituals eliminate entire categories of errors and decision fatigue. Plans to create shell aliases to reduce typing (gitsync for checkout + pull). Demonstrated this workflow successfully in hands-on exercise.

testing_after_merge.notes: NEW SKILL. Understanding of critical post-merge testing principle: never merge without verifying functionality. Recognition that resolved conflicts might: run perfectly, have syntax errors (leftover conflict markers), have logical errors (changes conflict when combined), break tests (incompatible changes). Post-merge testing checklist understood: visual inspection of resolved files, grep for leftover conflict markers, run application, check for console errors, run automated tests (when available), manual smoke test of affected features. Understanding that testing catches integration issues that weren't obvious during conflict resolution. Concept understood, needs to become automatic habit through repetition.

github_pr_merge_interface.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete understanding of GitHub PR merge interface: green 'Merge pull request' button with dropdown for three strategies (Create merge commit, Squash and merge, Rebase and merge). Successfully executed squash-and-merge in hands-on exercise. Understanding of customizing squash commit message (GitHub pre-fills with PR title and all commits, can edit to clean message). Recognition that GitHub option to delete branch after merge prevents manual cleanup. Understanding that merge via GitHub interface is preferred over local command-line merge for team collaboration and PR documentation preservation.

conflict_synthesis.notes: NEW SKILL. Exceptional understanding that best conflict resolutions often combine both versions rather than choosing binary winner. Key insight from intentional conflict exercise: 'sometimes the correct decision isn't binary (one is right and the other is wrong). Sometimes the best decision is a combination of both changes.' Successfully synthesized README conflict by combining 'AI-powered fishing journal' (feature branch) with 'automatically logs your catches' (main) plus additional context. Understanding of when to synthesize (both add different value, one has better structure/other better content) vs when to choose (typos, bugs, outdated code). Recognition that collaborative conflicts often represent convergent problem-solving where two valid approaches should be integrated. This demonstrates mature engineering judgment beyond typical junior-level binary thinking.
